s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques, ongoing for 2 weeks, in the context of immunotherapy
salient_findings: Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic annular erythema (EAE)
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils

shortlist.label: Wells syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Eosinophilic cellulitis with similar clinical and histopathological features to the patient's presentation

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Annular erythema with centrifugal spread, consistent with the patient's rash description

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Annular plaques with granulomatous inflammation, although less likely given the eosinophilic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Drug-induced erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Temporal association with immunotherapy initiation and clinical presentation consistent with drug-induced erythema annulare centrifugum

raw.rationale: The presence of numerous eosinophils in the biopsy and the clinical presentation of erythematous annular plaques without scale are consistent with Eosinophilic annular erythema (EAE), which is a rare condition characterized by annular erythema with eosinophilic infiltration.

rejected.label: Wells syndrome
rejected.why: While Wells syndrome also involves eosinophilic infiltration, it typically presents with cellulitis-like features, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: This condition can present with similar annular plaques, but the biopsy findings of numerous eosinophils are more suggestive of EAE.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: Granuloma annulare typically presents with papular lesions that coalesce into annular plaques, but the biopsy findings in this case do not show the characteristic granulomatous inflammation.

rejected.label: Drug-induced erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: While the patient is receiving immunotherapy, the biopsy findings and clinical presentation are more consistent with EAE than a drug-induced reaction.
